findings_qualitative.value: CO emission lies only outside the 6 cm radio lobe but inside the X-ray shock, while Halpha is present on both sides.

evidence.quote: CO emission is *only* observed outside of the radio lobe.

findings_qualitative.value: M87 is cold-gas poor given its Halpha flux compared with other cluster central galaxies.

evidence.quote: M87 indeed appears very cold-gas poor given the H$\alpha$ flux measurements presented here.

claims.hypothesis: Is molecular gas detectable in the M87 filament?
claims.experiment: ALMA Band 6 CO(2-1) observation of the field 40" SE of the nucleus
claims.finding: First secure detection of molecular gas in M87

evidence.quote: representing the first secure detection of molecular gas in the brightest cluster galaxy of the nearest cool-core cluster

claims.hypothesis: Does the AGN radio lobe or shock affect the molecular gas?
claims.experiment: Compare CO and Halpha inside and outside the radio lobe
claims.result: Halpha/CO ratio changes by factor >5 across the lobe edge
claims.finding: AGN lobe or shock destroys or excites the molecular gas

evidence.quote: Hence, the H$\alpha$ to CO(2–1) ratio changes by a factor of more than 5 across the edge of the radio lobe.

claims.hypothesis: Is the molecular gas dynamically quiescent?
claims.result: sigma = 27±3 km/s, an order of magnitude below the [CII] velocity gradient

evidence.quote: is consistent with a predominantly laminar dynamical structure of these filaments

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Coincidence of X-ray shock with CO dimming in 3D judged unlikely; a time lag after shock passage remains possible.

evidence.quote: We conclude that it is unlikely that the X-ray shock coincides in 3D geometry with the dimming of CO(2–1) emission observed with ALMA.

limitations_admitted.value: Mass is subject to large systematic uncertainty from the assumed Galactic XCO.

evidence.quote: albeit with large uncertainties related to the assumption that the CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor is similar to that in our own Galaxy

referee_caveats_inferred: Single pointing covers only a small part of the filament
Interpretation (lobe vs shock) depends on poorly known 3D geometry
Flux errors and the CO(2-1)/(1-0) ratio assumption are weakly justified
Only an upper limit inside the lobe, with no search for higher-J lines
